n0.hypothesis: Improve multi-resolution chord recognition on development recordings while identifying whether resolution, harmonic contamination, or boundary timing limits fusion.
n0.insight:
[from n1] Increasing the short window improves its evidence, but combining it with8192adds little. Test whether low-frequency resolution of the long window is limiting.
[from n2] The fixed local-median whitening suppresses useful spectral balance in this setup; do not stack it into later variants.
[from n3] Boundary movement can improve timing metrics while leaving most chord-label errors unchanged; prioritize representation accuracy.
[from n4] Development gains remain small despite varying resolution, whitening and boundary refinement; preserve the baseline and use external data to test the modest fixed-fusion candidate.
[from n1] A fixed fusion gain on development recordings is insufficient evidence of transfer: the separate64-recording comparison favours the single long window.

n1.hypothesis: A4096-sample short window supplies more reliable chord evidence than2048 samples and improves fixed or confidence-weighted fusion with8192 samples.
n1.insight: The small development fusion gain did not transfer to the external corpus. Keep8192singlewindow; investigate errors shared by both views and the no-chord rule.

n3.insight: Boundary movement can improve timing metrics while leaving most chord-label errors unchanged; prioritize representation accuracy.
